TermTranslation.definition: Using tests and exams on a regular basis to watch for changes in a person’s health.
A treatment used after the standard treatment to reduce the risk of cancer coming back.
A treatment used instead of the currently accepted and widely used treatment.
A drug that makes pain go away.
The loss of feeling or numbing of pain in some or all of the body.
A drug that prevents or stops vomiting.
Something, such as a drug, that prevents or stops inflammation.
A drug that fights infection.
Something made by the immune system to fight disease.
Anything, such as bacteria or a virus, that triggers the body’s immune response.
A treatment that uses natural or artificial materials to kill, control or change the way cells behave.
A treatment that gives chemotherapy during the same time period as radiation therapy.
A treatment that uses drugs to kill or destroy cancer cells.
A research study that tests new ways to prevent, detect, treat or manage a disease on people.
A treatment that uses more than one type of treatment at the same time.
The currently accepted and widely used treatment for a disease.
Someone who gives blood, cells, tissues or an organ to be used in another person.
The amount of a drug or radiation given at one time.
A treatment that uses medical drugs to treat a disease.
A drug that is being tested to find out if it works and is safe, but that is not yet approved for use.
Keeping track of a person’s health for a period of time after treatment to watch for problems or for signs that the disease has come back.
In the original site or place.
When a person learns the potential risks, benefits and limits of a procedure, treatment, clinical trial or test before deciding to participate.
Using a needle and syringe to push fluids or drugs into the body.
A disease or tumour that cannot be treated with an operation.
Within or into a vein.
A disease that grows into surrounding tissue.
A test or tool that breaks the skin or enters a body cavity.
Losing interest in food and not eating.
A drug that makes very bad pain go away.
A disease that is only in one place.
A test or tool that does not break the skin or enter a body cavity.
The study of cancers, including development, diagnosis, treatment and prevention.
A disease or tumour that can be treated with an operation.
The study of disease, including causes, development and effects on the body.
A treatment that use special exercises, activities and massage to treat pain, disease or injury.
The chance of recovery or of a disease coming back.
A treatment that uses high-energy rays or particles, such as x-rays, to damage or destroy cancer cells.
A disease that has come back after a period of time when there were no signs or symptoms of disease.
A period of time when the signs and symptoms of a disease get better or go away.
The chance of getting a disease.
A drug or a substance made by the body, such as a hormone, that affects how the body works.
An operation to look for disease or to remove or repair tissue, an organ or a part of the body.
Any treatment that mainly kills cancer cells with little or no effect on normal cells.
Putting blood or blood products into the body through a vein.
A treatment that uses an antigen to trigger the immune system to make antibodies that fight a disease.
